title: On the Number of Distinct Topological Bases of a Finite Set of Size $N$
summary: For a finite set $S$ with $\lvert S\rvert = N$, the number of families $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(S)$ that are topological bases is $\#(N) = \sum_{\mathcal{T} \in \operatorname{Top}(S)} 2^{\lvert\mathcal{T}\rvert - \lvert\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}}\rvert}$, where $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}}$ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighborhoods. The identity is proved in Lean 4 / Mathlib (`CARDB.lean`): bases generating $\mathcal{T}$ are exactly the sets with $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}} \subseteq \mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$.
